mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint recent-vs-all-prior divergence for BOTH teams simultaneously: Team B shots FOR (recent 21.2 vs all-prior 12.9) and shots_on_target FOR (recent 8.0 vs all-prior 4.8) rising sharply, while Team A shots AGAINST (recent 16.4 vs all-prior 13.2) and shots_on_target AGAINST (recent 5.0 vs all-prior 4.6) also rising. The mechanism requires both observables and both team perspectives to be evaluated jointly.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When one team's recent shot-generation across both shots and shots-on-target rises above its long-run mean while the opponent's recent shot-suppression deteriorates across both observables, total match shots and shots-on-target rise above competition baseline
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's recent surge in shots and shots-on-target (FOR) coincides with a simultaneous collapse in shots allowed (AGAINST), while Team A's shots FOR have declined recently and shots AGAINST have risen. The joint relationship between one team's shot-generation trend and the opponent's shot-suppression trend — measured across both observables simultaneously for both sides — captures a structural mismatch not reducible to either observable alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a joint condition across two distinct observables (shots AND shots_on_target) for two sides simultaneously — it cannot be reduced to a single observable with one conditioning band. The asymmetric divergence pattern (one team's FOR rising, opponent's AGAINST also rising) is a two-observable, two-perspective joint structure.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where one team holds materially above-50% possession (both all-prior and recent) AND that same team's offsides FOR are elevated relative to its own all-prior mean and relative to the opponent's offsides FOR. Evaluate whether possession dominance combined with elevated offside rate co-occurs systematically.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team's possession share rises above competition baseline and its recent offsides FOR diverge upward from its own long-run mean, total match offsides rise above competition context baseline
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B holds dominant possession (all-prior ~55%, recent ~62%) while Team A concedes possession (~54% all-prior, ~49% recent). Team B's offsides FOR have spiked recently (recent 3.2 vs all-prior 1.8), suggesting that high-possession, high-tempo forward play generates elevated offside counts. The joint relationship between possession dominance and offside frequency — across both teams — is a two-observable mechanism.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Requires jointly conditioning on two distinct observables (possession AND offsides) for the same team, with the possession level acting as a continuous modifier of the offside relationship — not a coarse band on a single observable.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where Team A's fouls FOR exceeds Team B's fouls FOR, AND Team B's cards_2h AGAINST exceeds Team A's cards_2h AGAINST. Measure whether the team that commits more fouls against a high-card-conceding opponent generates elevated second-half cards for that opponent.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When the fouling rate of one team (FOR) is elevated relative to the opponent's fouling rate, and the opponent's cards_2h AGAINST rate is also elevated, total second-half cards rise above competition context baseline
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A commits more fouls FOR (all-prior 12.9, away 13.0) than Team B (all-prior 12.1), while Team B concedes more fouls AGAINST (all-prior 13.5) than Team A concedes AGAINST (all-prior 10.6). Simultaneously, Team A's cards_2h FOR (1.32) exceeds Team B's cards_2h FOR (1.23), and Team B's cards_2h AGAINST (1.53) exceeds Team A's cards_2h AGAINST (1.08). The joint relationship between the foul-committing rate of one team and the second-half card rate of the opponent — across both observables and both perspectives — is an asymmetric cross-team mechanism.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is an asymmetric cross-team joint mechanism: it requires simultaneously reading one team's fouls FOR against the other team's cards_2h AGAINST — two distinct observables across two different team perspectives. This cannot be reduced to a single observable with one conditioning band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the within-match half split of corner_kicks FOR and AGAINST for both teams simultaneously. Specifically, evaluate whether the team whose corner production is back-loaded (higher 2H than 1H rate) faces an opponent whose corner-conceding rate is also back-loaded, amplifying second-half corner totals relative to first-half corner totals.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both teams show a back-loaded corner profile (higher 2H than 1H rates for corners FOR and/or AGAINST), second-half corner totals exceed first-half corner totals by more than the competition baseline half-split would predict
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A generates corners more heavily in the second half (FOR 2H: 2.19 vs 1H: 1.79) while Team B generates corners more heavily in the first half (FOR 1H: 2.27 vs 2H: 2.56, but AGAINST 1H: 1.60 vs 2H: 2.08). The within-match half-level distribution of corner production differs structurally between the two teams, creating an asymmetric half-by-half corner profile that cannot be captured by full-match totals alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a within-match half-level split (1H vs 2H) applied jointly to both teams' FOR and AGAINST corner profiles simultaneously — a two-half, two-perspective joint structure. It is not reducible to a single observable at full-match level with one conditioning band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on: (a) the within-match half split of goals FOR and AGAINST for both teams, and (b) the possession dominance level of the attacking team. Evaluate whether teams with possession above a threshold show a different 1H-vs-2H goal distribution than teams with balanced or below-average possession.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team holds possession materially above competition baseline, its second-half goals FOR rate rises relative to its first-half goals FOR rate, and this half-skew is more pronounced than for teams with balanced possession
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B scores more goals in the second half (FOR 2H: 0.91) than the first half (FOR 1H: 0.67), while Team A concedes more in the first half (AGAINST 1H: 0.67) than the second half (AGAINST 2H: 0.76) — but Team B holds dominant possession (recent ~62%). The joint relationship between possession dominance and the within-match half-level goal distribution — specifically whether high-possession teams convert their dominance into goals more in one half than the other — is a two-observable, within-match-state mechanism.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on possession level (a continuous observable) and the within-match half-level split of goals — two distinct observables with a within-match state dimension. It is not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band.
